# Stand-up rhythm

The daily stand-up works as a rhythm, not as a status report. Same time, same place, fifteen minutes at most. Each person says what moved, what is stuck and what they need. When the team skips two days in a row, the rhythm breaks and the next meeting turns into a long catch-up that nobody enjoys.

I feed the habit with small rituals: the first speaker rotates, the board is updated before the meeting, and blockers get an owner on the spot. A steady daily cadence keeps small problems small and makes the team's pace visible to everyone.

If the meeting grows past fifteen minutes, split it or drop the topics that belong elsewhere.
